diagnosis_explanation: Your child has a urinary tract infection. It was caused by a germ called Pseudomonas. This germ can make a person feel sick. Your child also has high blood pressure. This is called hypertension. Their kidneys are not working as well as they should. This is called chronic renal insufficiency. Your child was born with only one kidney. This kidney is on the left side. It has a blockage. This is called an obstruction.
medication_rationale:
Macrodantin:
This medicine helps prevent urinary tract infections. Your child has a single kidney. It is important to protect that kidney. Your child may have an upset stomach. This medicine can make your child's urine look darker. This is normal. Call your doctor if your child gets a rash or has trouble breathing.

Enalapril:
This medicine helps lower your child's high blood pressure. It helps the kidneys work better. Your child might have a dry cough. This is expected. Your child could feel dizzy. Call your doctor if your child's face or lips swell. Also call if the cough is very bothersome.

Hydralazine:
This medicine helps lower your child's blood pressure. It can also help with urine flow. Your child might get a headache. They may also feel dizzy. This is often mild. Call your doctor if your child feels very tired. Also call if they have chest pain.

Lasix:
This medicine helps your child's body get rid of extra fluid. This helps the kidneys and blood pressure. Your child will urinate more often. This is normal. Your child might feel dizzy. Call your doctor if your child gets muscle cramps. Also call if your child's heart beats very fast.

Fortaz:
This medicine fights a type of bacteria causing your child's infection. It helps clear up the urinary tract infection. Your child may have diarrhea. This is common. Your child might get a rash. Call your doctor if your child gets hives or trouble breathing.

Ciprofloxacin:
This medicine fights bacteria causing your child's infection. It helps clear up the urinary tract infection. Your child may have an upset stomach or diarrhea. These are often mild. Your child could get dizzy or feel sleepy. Call your doctor right away if your child has severe stomach pain. Also call if they have swelling in their joints.
Important: Do not stop taking this medicine without calling your doctor first.
Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- Your child may feel tired and uncomfortable after the procedures.
- Keep your child resting most of the day.
- Watch for fever, vomiting, or increased pain.
- Call your doctor if your child has trouble breathing.
- Your child cannot have anything by mouth except clear liquids today.
- Your child can have a light meal of soft foods tonight.
- Your child's goal is to drink small sips of clear liquids often.
- Your child must not have salt added to food.

**Week 2:**
- Your child may have less pain and more energy this week.
- Your child can start doing light activities around the house.
- Keep your child from running or jumping.
- Do not let your child lift anything heavy.
- Your child can eat a regular diet. Do not add salt to food.
- Watch for signs of infection like fever or cloudy urine.
- Call your doctor if your child has pain when urinating.
- Your child's goal is to drink fluids well between meals.

**Week 3:**
- Your child should feel more like themselves this week.
- Your child can increase activity slowly. Avoid rough play.
- Do not let your child lift anything over 5 pounds.
- Make sure your child takes all prescribed medicines.
- Monitor your child for any signs of infection.
- Call your doctor if your child has a high fever.
- Your child's goal is to walk around the house more each day.
- Avoid foods high in salt.

**Week 4:**
- Your child should have good energy levels this week.
- Your child can do most normal activities but still no rough play.
- Continue to avoid lifting heavy items.
- Your child's goal is to walk outside for short periods.
- Watch for any changes in your child's urine.
- Call your doctor if your child has back pain or swelling.
- Keep salt intake low.
- Ensure your child drinks plenty of fluids.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your child's symptoms should get better over the next few weeks.
- Keep your child on a low-salt diet long term.
- Ensure your child takes all medications as directed.
- Follow up with all scheduled doctor appointments.
- Monitor your child for any signs of a urinary tract infection.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Breathing trouble or gasping: Your child needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain or pressure: This is a medical emergency.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: Apply pressure now.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking.
- Seizure or loss of consciousness: Call for help right now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 F (38.5 C) that is not going down: Your child may have an infection.
- Your child cannot keep fluids down: They need help staying hydrated.
- New and worsening confusion: This needs urgent medical review.
- Sudden bad pain in your child's leg: This could be a blood clot.
- Wound looks infected, red streaks, warm to touch: This needs to be seen.
- Sudden weight gain of 2+ lbs in one day: Fluid may be building up fast.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Your child has mild pain: This should get better slowly.
- Your child's wound is healing slowly: Watch for infection signs.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while healing.
- Questions about your child's medicine: Your doctor can help you.
